# Modifier-Primacy Status — Repository vs. Specification

**What this document is:** a from-scratch audit of how far the current repository (`d:\Utilities\XAMPP\htdocs\dndchar`) is from `docs/architecture/modifier-primacy.md`, generated by checking each rule in that specification directly against the schema, service layer, types, and UI. Where the spec and this document disagree about what the target model *should be*, the spec wins — this document only reports distance to that target.

**Methodology:** every numbered rule in `modifier-primacy.md` §2–§6 was checked against the live code (migrations 001–018, `src/lib/server/services/*`, `src/lib/types/*`, `src/lib/rules/dnd5e.ts`, and the admin/character UI). Citations are file path + line number. This is a full regeneration, not an edit of any prior version — prior findings were used only as a starting checklist, not trusted as still-true.

This document supersedes the narrower, narrative `modifier-primacy-audit.md` in this same directory, which was generated against an earlier, less-precise revision of the spec and is now stale in places (see §6 below for what changed).

---

## 0. Things to flag before the findings

**Doc-hierarchy discrepancy — resolved.** At the time this document was first generated, the repo had two `CLAUDE.md` files (root and `docs/architecture/CLAUDE.md`) and only the nested one referenced this status document or stated the "spec always wins" rule. The root `CLAUDE.md` — the one its own first line says is "read automatically at the start of every session" — has since been updated to match: it now points to `modifier-primacy.md` as the flat spec and this file as the status snapshot, in that order, and states the same "spec wins, status only reports distance" rule. No further action needed here; noted only so this document's own history is traceable.

**Spec claims that assume something not true of the codebase:**
- §2.1 and the Open Questions list both refer to **Soulfire** and **Vowfire** as if they were existing, confirmed resource pools ("campaign-specific pools such as Soulfire and Vowfire"). Neither exists anywhere in code — no `modifier_targets` row, no resource table, no string literal. They are entirely aspirational; the spec's phrasing ("such as") reads as if pointing at something already real.
- §5.2's worked example talks about "Rage (the class feature)" and "Raging (the state)" as two distinct things, as though this distinction already exists in the project's content and the spec is just formalizing it. The actual seed data (`scripts/seed-core-effects.ts`) has exactly one `Rage` row with its modifiers attached directly — there is no `Raging` entity today, in any form. This isn't just an engine gap; it implies content needs to be re-modeled as two pieces, not only that the engine needs a new capability.
- §3.1's stacking table states "2 advantage + 1 disadvantage = net 1 advantage" as the confirmed rule. Standard 5e rules don't have degrees of advantage — any single source of disadvantage cancels all sources of advantage, regardless of count. The spec is deliberately choosing a non-standard, count-based rule; worth flagging only because the current code actually implements the *standard* cancellation rule (see §3.1 below), so this is a real, not cosmetic, behavioral divergence to resolve, not just an implementation gap.

---

## 1. Fully Conforms

Rules where the live code already does what the spec requires, with no reshaping needed.

- **§2.1 — Modifier definition carries no duration, cost, or instance-source.** `modifier_definitions` (migration `006_normalize_modifiers.sql:1-10`) holds only `target`, `modifier_type`, `value_expression`(later `default_value_expression`, `008_homebrew_modifier_overhaul.sql:12-39`), `label`, `description`. Duration lives on `effect_definitions`/`active_character_effects`; cost-like fields live on `content_spell_access`/`action_steps`. None of that leaks onto the Modifier row itself.
- **§2.1 — Dot-notation target convention.** Confirmed throughout `scripts/seed-core-effects.ts` and `modifier_targets` seed data (`014_content_catalogue_and_time.sql:21-44`): `ability_check.str`, `attack_roll.all`, `damage_taken.bludgeoning`, etc.
- **§2.1 — Fixed and Dice value sources.** `default_value_expression` stores literal numbers (e.g. `'2'` for a flat AC bonus) and dice expressions (e.g. `'1d4'` for Bless, `004_modifier_engine.sql:105`) and both are consumed as-is by the roll/bonus resolution code.
- **§2.2 — Empty-grant ("purely descriptive") Containers.** `character_inventory_items.source_content_id` is nullable (`014_content_catalogue_and_time.sql:194`, `ON DELETE SET NULL`), and `replaceInventory` (`characters.ts:966-976`) inserts an item from name/category/quantity alone with no requirement to attach any content/effect/modifier. A "gold watch" with no mechanics is fully representable today.
- **§2.4 — Duration/lifecycle excluded from the Modifier.** Confirmed by the same evidence as the first bullet: `duration_type`, `duration_rounds`, `remaining_rounds`, `expires_at`, `expiry_boundary` all live on `effect_definitions`/`active_character_effects`, never on `modifier_definitions`.
- **§3.1 — Flat numeric add/subtract sums normally.** `resolvedNumericModifiers` (`dnd5e.ts:120-136`) flat-maps every matching modifier's resolved value and sums them with no special-casing; multiple `+1 AC` sources add as expected.
- **§4.2 — Mechanics always resolve against the live definition, never a frozen one.** `rule-engine.ts`'s `resolveCharacterModifierSources` queries `modifier_definitions`/`effect_modifier_links`/`content_modifier_links` directly every time it runs; there is no code path that reads a mechanic's behavior from anywhere but those live tables, including after a version restore (restore re-establishes rows that reference live definition IDs, not denormalized mechanic text).
- **§4.3 — Soft-delete only.** `is_archived` exists on `modifier_targets`, `modifier_definitions`, `effect_definitions`, `content_definitions`, `action_definitions` (all added in `016_rules_catalogue_redesign.sql`); no service code hard-deletes a definition row, only link/junction rows.
- **§4.5 — Update-in-place vs. fork-a-copy.** Both paths are real and wired end-to-end: `create`/`update`/`copy` actions in `src/routes/admin/rules/modifiers/+page.server.ts:6-8` all call `saveModifier(form, mode)` (`rules-admin.ts:104`); `update` is gated behind a `confirmShared` checkbox enforced server-side (`rules-admin.ts:113`); `copy` forks a new, independent definition.
- **§6.3 — A Container may attach multiple independent Modifier instances.** `ContentTypeAdmin.svelte`'s repeatable `?/attachModifier` form (lines ~91-104) adds one `content_modifier_links` row per submission; nothing limits a content record to a single modifier.

## 2. Partially Conforms (Needs Reshaping)

Rules where a real, working piece of the mechanism exists, but it's incomplete, scoped too narrowly, or built on the wrong underlying shape to fully satisfy the rule as written.

- **§2.1 — Modifier target categories.** Derived stats, roll categories, and discrete rules (crit threshold via `condition_expression`, advantage/disadvantage state) are all real and seeded. Resource-pool targets are *conceptually* supported by the dot-notation scheme but no actual resource-pool target exists beyond standard HP/spell-slots — Soulfire/Vowfire (named explicitly in the spec) have zero representation. Needs extending, not rebuilding.
- **§2.1 — Stat-derived formula value source.** `modifier_targets.value_kind` declares a `'formula'` kind and seeds entries like `proficiency_bonus`-style targets (`014_content_catalogue_and_time.sql:10-19, 44`), but `resolveModifierNumericValue` (`dnd5e.ts:113-118`) only ever evaluates one hardcoded literal string, `'rage_damage_bonus'` → `barbarianRageDamageBonus()`. There is no general formula evaluator (e.g. for `10 + dex_mod + con_mod`) — the schema gestures at this value source, the resolver doesn't implement it generically.
- **§2.2 — Container's component fields (name/description/source/activation_type/cost/duration/grants).** Every individual field exists somewhere — `effect_definitions` has name/description/duration; `content_modifier_links`/`content_effect_links` have `activation_type` (`carried`/`equipped`/`attuned`/`known`/`prepared`/`manual`); `content_definitions` has `source_kind`/`source_ref` — but they're scattered across `effect_definitions`, `content_definitions`, and their link tables rather than living on one shape. The fields the spec wants on a Container exist; the single Container they're meant to live on does not (see §4, Direct Conflicts).
- **§2.5 — Source and target-of-effect tracked independently.** The schema is ready: `active_character_effects.source_character_id` (`004_modifier_engine.sql:33`) and `source_key` (`016_rules_catalogue_redesign.sql:212-213`) both exist and can record a source distinct from the affected character. But no UI (no target/party-member picker found anywhere in the Svelte components) and no service code (`effects.ts`'s `applyCharacterEffect`, lines 9-36, takes only `characterId` + `effectId`, no separate target parameter) actually exercises this. The data model supports the rule; nothing populates it that way today.
- **§2.6 — Audit trail for every resolved value.** Real and working for combat: `rollDamageExpression` (`CharacterSheetForm.svelte:484-532`) builds a labelled `lines[]` breakdown (dice rolls, flat bonuses, ability modifier, each modifier's `.label`, running totals, final `Total:`). The spec is explicit that this "applies uniformly to every calculated value, not only combat rolls" — AC, saving throws, and skill checks have no equivalent breakdown UI anywhere. The pattern exists and is provably good; it needs extending to every other derived value, not redesigning.
- **§3.1 — Advantage/disadvantage stacking.** `resolveAdvantageState` (`dnd5e.ts:151-158`) does collect every matching modifier and produce a single net result, and it is scoped to whatever `candidates` target list the caller passes in (so it can be roll-category-scoped if called correctly) — partial conformance with the "per-bucket" requirement. But see §4 (Direct Conflicts) for how its actual cancellation logic differs from the spec's stated rule.
- **§6.1 — Grant-free Container creation by "players."** The underlying data shape is there (see §1's empty-grant bullet) and *technically* anyone can create one — but since there is no role/permission enforcement at all (§3, Missing Entirely), there's no actual "players may, DM/admin may not" distinction happening; everyone can currently do everything, including the things the spec wants gated to DM/admin. The shape conforms; the gating that makes it meaningful does not exist.

---

## 3. Missing Entirely

Rules with no trace anywhere in schema, services, or UI — not a partial implementation, nothing to extend.

- **§2.1 — Derived-from-sibling value source.** No column, no resolver branch, nothing resembling reading one modifier's value from a sibling modifier on the same record. Crit-bonus damage (the spec's own canonical example) doesn't exist in any form — neither "roll an extra die" nor "add the die's max as a flat bonus."
- **§2.3 — Structured cost list (`[{ pool, amount }]`).** Every cost-shaped field found (`content_spell_access.resource_cost_expression`, `action_steps.value_expression`) is a single scalar/string column. No multi-pool, multi-line cost representation exists anywhere, and since Soulfire/Vowfire pools don't exist either, there's nothing yet to even attach a second cost line to.
- **§2.4 — Expiry side-effects as a grant-on-trigger.** No `'expired'`/`on_expire` trigger type was found anywhere (`action_steps.trigger_type` supports `on_use`/`manual`/`on_cast` only). A Container that fires something specific when it wears off (the spec's Haste-lethargy example) has no mechanism.
- **§3.1 — Resistance/vulnerability per-damage-type netting.** No code anywhere nets resistance against vulnerability per damage type, or at all. `resolvedNumericModifiers`/`resolveAdvantageState` cover advantage/disadvantage only; nothing analogous exists for resistance/vulnerability.
- **§3.1 — "Doesn't stack with itself" flag.** No per-modifier-definition boolean for this exists. The adjacent, differently-scoped `effect_definitions.stack_behavior` enum (`'refresh'`/`'stack'`/`'reject'`, `016_rules_catalogue_redesign.sql:23-24`) controls whether *re-applying the same effect* refreshes/stacks/rejects — a related but distinct problem (effect-level re-application, not modifier-level stacking exceptions) — and it's checked in `effects.ts`'s `effectApplicationDecision`, not in any per-modifier resolution path.
- **§3.1 — Resource-grant-sums-by-count (the `luck_dice` pattern).** Nothing resembling a countable resource grant that sums across sources exists. `character_content_resources`/`character_inventory_resources` track a single current/max value per resource definition, not multiple independently-sourced grants of the same resource that need summing.
- **§5 (all of it) — Containers granting other Containers.** Confirmed with certainty: no `effect_grants` table, no self-referencing FK on `effect_definitions`, and `content_grants` only links `content_definitions` → `content_definitions` (item/feat/spell/class_feature granting other catalogue content), never effect → effect. `rule-engine.ts`'s grant resolution (lines ~79-94) walks exactly one hop and stops; there is no recursive/chained grant resolution anywhere. Since there is also no unified Container, this entire section has no structural home to attach to yet — it isn't just an unbuilt feature, the concept it depends on (§2.2's Container) doesn't exist either.
- **§6.1 — Permission tiers.** Confirmed twice independently: a `role: 'user' | 'admin'` column exists on the user/session model (`014_content_catalogue_and_time.sql:1-8`), but no route handler or service function checks it. Grepping every `admin/**/+page.server.ts` and every relevant service (`content-admin.ts`, `rules-admin.ts`) for `role`, `'admin'`, or any authorization guard returns nothing. An `authorization.ts` file exists under `src/lib/server/auth/` but is not imported anywhere. Any authenticated user can currently author/edit modifiers, effects, and content.
- **§6.4 — Two-phase roll resolution for outcome-dependent conditions.** No crit detection, no threshold check, no conditional gating of damage modifiers on the to-hit result. `rollBattleAction` calls `rollDamageExpression` immediately and unconditionally; there's no "first phase" to speak of.
- **§4.4 — Version-history drift display.** `VersionList.svelte` renders `changeSummary` and a restore button per snapshot and nothing else; `getCharacterVersions`/`restoreCharacterVersion` (`characters.ts:316-320, 334-363`) have no logic that compares a snapshot's referenced definitions against their current live state. The character-state-diff/definition-drift distinction the spec requires doesn't exist in any form — there isn't even an undifferentiated combined diff, just a static label and a restore action.

---

## 4. Direct Conflicts

Rules where the current code doesn't just lack the feature — it actively does something structurally or behaviorally different from what the spec requires.

- **§2.2 — Single Container concept.** This is the central, load-bearing conflict the rest of the document traces back to. The live schema is not "one Container shape distinguished only by metadata" — it is four genuinely different shapes: `effect_definitions` (+`effect_modifier_links`), `content_definitions` joined to *type-specific* tables `spell_definitions`/`item_definitions`, and a fully separate `action_definitions`/`action_steps` execution engine. Items and Spells are not the same schema with different metadata; they are different tables with different columns, joined through a shared parent row. No code path treats them interchangeably. Every other "missing" or "partial" finding in this document involving Containers (§2.3, §2.4's expiry grants, §5 entirely, parts of §6.1) is downstream of this one.
- **§3.1 — Advantage/disadvantage cancellation rule.** The spec explicitly states sources should be counted and netted serially (its own example: "2 advantage + 1 disadvantage = net 1 advantage"). The actual code, `resolveAdvantageState` (`dnd5e.ts:151-158`), does not count sources — if both an advantage-granting and a disadvantage-granting modifier are present, it returns `'normal'` regardless of how many of each exist, which is the standard 5e cancellation rule, not the spec's count-based rule. This is a behavioral disagreement between a written rule and working code, not an absence.
- **§6.2 — Authoring/applying must not share a tab set or screen.** `CharacterSheetForm.svelte`'s `modifierFilters` array (lines 119-130) lists `'catalogue'` as one of ten co-equal tab options — `Active/Automated/Potential/Condition/Spell/Combat/Class/Environment/All/Catalogue` — all on the same player-facing panel (confirmed live at line 170: `modifierFilter === 'catalogue'` is a real, reachable filter branch). This is the opposite of "the two functions do not share a tab set or a single screen": today they share both the tab set and the screen.

## 5. What changed since the prior audit (`modifier-primacy-audit.md`)

That document was written against an earlier spec revision and is now stale in a few specific ways, beyond simply being supplanted by this one:

- Its biggest finding — that §6.4 of the *old* spec claimed the Catalogue tab "is removed" as an already-completed fact when it demonstrably wasn't — no longer applies as a "the doc is wrong about its own state" problem, because the current spec (§6.2) states the separation as a present-tense requirement rather than a past-tense claim. The underlying code fact is unchanged (the tab is still there), but it's now a clean, ordinary Direct Conflict rather than evidence the previous spec was misreporting its own research.
- The prior audit treated the copy-vs-update Modifier UI (§4.5) as only partially confirmed ("NOT FULLY VERIFIED... the route handler isn't shown"). This audit confirms it directly: `modifiers/+page.server.ts:8` wires a `copy` action to `saveModifier(form, 'copy')`, and `rules-admin.ts:104`'s function signature explicitly accepts `'copy'` as a third mode alongside `'create'`/`'update'`. It is fully implemented, not partial.
- The prior audit didn't check value-source types, the cross-character targeting schema, per-bucket netting internals, the "doesn't stack with itself" flag, or version-history drift display at all — those are new findings in this document, not updates to old ones.
